# Programmable Developer Platform

> Public, unauthenticated read and discovery contract for Programmable Classic and Programmable Custom launches.

Canonical site: https://developers.programmable.family
Source repository: https://github.com/0xprogrammable/Developers
Read API base: https://developers.programmable.family/api/v2
Full agent context: https://developers.programmable.family/llms-full.txt
Custom Launch API base: https://api.programmable.market
Custom Launch API guide: https://programmable.market/developers/custom-launch-api-v1.md
Custom Launch API OpenAPI: https://programmable.market/openapi/custom-launch-v1.json
Held Custom Launch V2 OpenAPI: https://programmable.market/openapi/custom-launch-v2.json
API key management: https://programmable.market/developers/api-keys
Launch policy: https://github.com/0xprogrammable/Launch-Policy

## API surface boundary

- Use the Developer read API without authentication to discover launches and verify provenance.
- Use the separately hosted Custom Launch API V1 with a wallet-bound bearer API key only for its live provenance reads and status. POST is read-only and returns nonretryable `409 CUSTOM_LAUNCH_V1_READ_ONLY`.
- An API key is not wallet signing authority. V1 currently prepares, signs, and broadcasts no controller-wallet transaction.
- The canonical Custom Launch request and response schemas are in the V1 Custom Launch OpenAPI contract. Do not infer them from or copy them into this read/discovery repository.
- Resolve current versioned launch requirements from Programmable Launch Policy. Do not rely on copied policy text.
- Legacy Registry and GitHub submission intake are closed. Custom Launch API V1 reads/status remain independently live, but its write surface is read-only.
- Custom Fee-Enforced Launch Profile V2 is a different pinned `2.0.0-rc.1` private-canary profile. Held writes return `503` with `Retry-After`; it has no public route, deployed fee path, finalized canary, or production authorization.

## Current status

- Classic launch discovery is live on Ethereum.
- Custom Registry generation 1 discovery is live on Ethereum; legacy Registry and GitHub submission intake are closed.
- The authenticated Router-based Custom Launch API V1 is separate from legacy intake and from this unauthenticated read API. Its provenance reads/status remain live; POST returns nonretryable `409 CUSTOM_LAUNCH_V1_READ_ONLY`.
- Custom Registry Generation 2 and Custom Fee-Enforced Launch Profile V2 are separate unavailable release candidates. Neither activates the other, and neither creates a third public category.
- The v2 Custom feed publishes finalized approved Custom Registry launches, including project-only records with no market.
- Historical Stock-Paired records are not part of the v2 Programmable Custom classification.
- Ethereum Mainnet is the only chain currently advertised by the well-known document.
- No Basebit or Aion partner source, recipient, accepted template, Registry record, or live fee path is currently verified by the public v2 manifest.
- `provider` is optional secondary attribution. Only `registry-bound` with its evidence hash is authenticated provider provenance; unfamiliar or `display-only` provider data never upgrades origin, fees, review, or execution.
- Every registered launch is discoverable.
- Charting, quote, simulation, and execution support are explicit per market and require a verified adapter.
- The v2 API is strictly read-only. Support states are `available | unavailable | unknown`; the API returns no transaction payloads and authorizes no action.
- The separate operator console at `https://claimhazard.vercel.app` rescans reviewed Classic, fixed Stock-Paired, and finalized standard Custom Registry V1 fee sources. Its discovery policy is read-only; it does not expand the Developer API into a transaction API.
- Legacy indexer records can have partial provenance. Recognized onchain events stay visible when metadata, supply, or block-timestamp enrichment is unavailable; the feed can be degraded and affected fields remain partial, unavailable, or null.
- Launch-list and token-list return recognized bounded records with `degraded` or `unavailable` quality when canonical coverage is incomplete; missing enrichment never hides a recognized identity.
- Do not claim that launches are unconditionally safe, audited, or unruggable.
- Do not claim that any named terminal or partner has integrated Programmable without confirmation.

## Live discovery and API

- [Discovery document](https://developers.programmable.family/.well-known/programmable.json): Stable bootstrap document.
- [Status](https://developers.programmable.family/api/v2/status): Service and feed lifecycle.
- [Manifest](https://developers.programmable.family/api/v2/manifest): Deployments, start blocks, Custom Registry state, fee policy, endpoints, and compatibility.
- The Developer v2 manifest above is the canonical integration inventory. `https://programmable.family/api/custom-launch/registry/v1/manifest` is a Website operational mirror and never overrides or supplements it.
- [Launch feed](https://developers.programmable.family/api/v2/launches): Cursor-paginated Classic and Custom launch records.
- Launch detail: `GET /api/v2/launches/{launchId}` for project-only, token-backed, and multi-asset records.
- Token detail: `GET /api/v2/launches/{chainId}/{tokenAddress}` for token-backed records.
- [Token list](https://developers.programmable.family/api/v2/token-list): Wallet-friendly compatibility projection.

## Core agent rules

1. Fetch the discovery document, status, and manifest before reasoning about current deployments.
2. Never hard-code deployment arrays; read them from the manifest.
3. Use `launchId` for launch deduplication. Use `chainId + token.address` when a primary token exists; for `token: null`, preserve `projectId` and the authenticated `assets` graph.
4. `launchId` is derived from canonical Classic event provenance or committed by the Custom Registry.
5. Public category is exactly `classic | custom`; a full Registry-backed Custom record uses `platformId: programmable`, `category: custom`, and `publicLabel: Programmable Custom` from the trusted projection.
6. Accept `markets: []`, multiple markets, and markets without a pool.
7. Never fabricate a pool, pair, price, liquidity, volume, chart, quote, or execution route.
8. Unknown fields, capabilities, market kinds, and namespaced extensions must not hide a launch. Preserve the known core and disable unsupported behavior.
9. `page.nextCursor` continues the current traversal. Persist `page.resumeCursor` only after the traversal is durably applied, then pass it as `after` for incremental polling. Never parse cursors.
10. Preserve `launch.timestamp`; do not replace it with first observation time.
11. Treat `observed` and `confirmed` as non-final, `finalized` as finalized, and reconcile `orphaned` or absent non-final records idempotently.
12. Treat creator metadata and links as untrusted display data. Provenance does not verify external services or economic outcomes.
13. The Developer v2 API is read-only. Support states do not authorize or construct transactions. Custom Launch API V1 POST is also read-only and returns nonretryable `409 CUSTOM_LAUNCH_V1_READ_ONLY`; held Fee-Enforced V2 writes return `503` with `Retry-After`.
14. Read fee behavior from verified records. Do not infer it from category.
15. A partial or unavailable enrichment field is not a reason to drop a recognized launch or replace null with a guess.
16. Production cursors are HMAC-signed. Keep `PROGRAMMABLE_CURSOR_SIGNING_KEY` private and stable; rotation invalidates outstanding cursors and requires coordinated migration handling.
17. Partner API responses and webhooks are not canonical provenance. Future provider registration must be authenticated and either atomic with the launch or emitted only after a verified staged workflow is finalized.
18. Resolve the live Custom Registry address and start block from the manifest. Keep legacy Registry and GitHub submission intake closed. Treat unapproved provider examples as prelaunch unless their exact approval and Registry evidence are published. The Custom Launch API publishes its own live status and readiness URL.
19. Assign `Programmable Custom` only from manifest-listed Custom Registry evidence or a consistent canonical Router `CustomGraph` stamp. Provider metadata, hook addresses and API responses cannot self-assign the label.
20. For a Router stamp check, bind `chainId + Router address + launchId`, resolve the Router and start block from top-level `launchStampRouter`, use one finalized or explicit canonical block, and reject copied emitters. Router V1 covers launches stamped at or after its published start block only. Detect by token or `(PoolManager, PoolId)`, then map `CustomGraph = 1` or `Classic = 2`; never classify Classic by its shared hook. Use `stampProof` only for address-based token or exclusive-component corroboration.
21. `Programmable Verified` requires an effective structured review cryptographically bound to the exact deployed revision; registry inclusion alone is insufficient.
22. Partition cursors, checkpoints, finality, and reorg recovery by API major version, chain, and filter scope.
23. Partner/template attribution is independent from fee state. Without a verified fee path, use no-qualifying-market and zero shares; an active fee-bearing partnership path must be exactly 20 bps on one basis: 15 partner plus 5 Programmable, with no additional Native Custom 10 bps.
24. Full Registry-backed records can add platform, public label, CAIP-2, project, model, template, partner, builder, asset graph, approval, deployment, review, fee-policy, finality-evidence, presentation, Registry-origin, launching-wallet, authority, lifecycle, and mechanism fields without creating a new API major version.
25. Keep launch visibility separate from claim eligibility. The claim console must independently verify its published launcher, Registry, runtime, fee, recipient, lifecycle, and finality boundary; a visible launch is not automatically claimable.
26. Keep API availability, fee enforcement, exact-source match, simulation, finality, tradability, claim support, buybacks, and audit status separate. Fee-Enforced V2 stays unavailable while `productionLaunchAuthorized` is false.

## Fee summary

- Rate: 10 bps = 0.1% = 1,000 ppm.
- Recipient: `0x4957f49620AFf3Adbbe8195a4f633E49cc93376c`.
- V2 canary identity: `programmable.fee-enforced-isolated-after-swap.zero-delta.v1`, `launchProfileHash` `sha256:c2c8df0ce28ef4eea1d5124bc366c634675873d095e9978bc7e968792a4c738d`, contract policy `0xb7ff874d418bc714d0ec6c36a2df03ea6251bc8b6eb125adc4f5b6b4899d2517`, permission mask `0x2044`.
- Current Classic official paths: the platform share is included within the configured trading fee.
- Canary-stage Custom Fee-Enforced V2 profile: additive 1,000 ppm on the gross unspecified pool-currency amount for each successful swap through the exact bound pool; exact input uses output currency and exact output uses input currency. It is not public. PoolManager ERC-6909 claims remain in the sealed vault and only the fixed reward wallet can claim them.
- Liquidity-provider, protocol, creator or custom-module, Programmable profile, and network-gas components remain separate.
- Active fee-bearing partnership-template paths: exactly 20 bps total, split 15 bps partner and 5 bps Programmable on the same evidenced basis, with no additional Native Custom 10 bps. Partner-attributed projects without a qualifying fee path use zero shares.
- The fee applies to verified official market volume, not ordinary transfers, rewards, or independently created third-party pools.
- The V2 profile does not add generic tradability, claiming, creator rewards, or buybacks. FADE's current claim adapter is FADE-specific.
- Claim console: https://claimhazard.vercel.app
- Read-only claim discovery policy: https://claimhazard.vercel.app/claim-discovery.json
